steps.heading: Vectorize, don't loop
steps.body: pandas is fastest when an operation runs once across a whole column (vectorized) rather than once per row. Plain arithmetic, boolean masks, .str, and groupby() are all vectorized; .apply(), .map() with a lambda, and iterrows() all fall back to slow, per-row Python calls.

steps.heading: Same result, different speed
steps.code:
df['revenue'] * 1.1                      # fast, vectorized
df['revenue'].apply(lambda x: x * 1.1)    # slow, one Python call per row
steps.output: # identical output, very different performance at scale
steps.caption: Reach for apply()/map() only when there's genuinely no vectorized equivalent.

steps.heading: Dtypes and assignment matter too
steps.body: category dtype and smaller numeric types (int32, downcast) cut memory for repetitive or over-sized columns. df.loc[condition, 'col'] = value is the safe way to assign conditionally, chained bracket assignment can silently do nothing or trigger a SettingWithCopyWarning.
